The Industry Brief

Edition No. 7Covering October 26 to November 1, 2026Published November 2, 2026

Toyota Builds Waymo's Robotaxi, Germany's Rough Quarter and the Canada Tariff Cliff

Toyota will build Waymo's next robotaxi in the plant it opened for the first Corolla, which turns 60 this week. Volkswagen lost €5.9 billion in a quarter as China slipped away from Germany's carmakers, a 50% tariff on Canadian-built cars is 2 months out, Ford's cheapest EV learned to power a house and GM finally said yes to hybrids.

By Margot Devries · 32 minute read

In this edition

  1. Toyota will build Waymo's next robotaxi in the plant it opened for the first Corolla
  2. Germany's carmakers have a China problem, and Volkswagen lost €5.9 billion in 3 months
  3. Ford's off-road trims pay the bills, and its $28,350 electric truck learns to power a house
  4. A 50% tariff on Canadian-built cars is 2 months away, unless there's a deal
  5. GM gets its biggest crossover plant ready for hybrids, and leaves the NYSE
  6. Rivian's smaller R2 becomes its best seller in its first full quarter
  7. America starts its first big rewrite of the tire rules in more than 20 years
  8. Aston Martin takes the roof off a 1,064-hp hybrid

Special News Spotlight: The Corolla turns 60, still the best-selling car of all time

The week's theme was who builds what, and where. Toyota will build Waymo's robotaxis on its own assembly line, Germany's carmakers are learning that China now builds the cars Chinese buyers would rather have, a tariff deadline could decide where some of America's best-selling cars are made, and GM is finally building the hybrids its dealers asked for. And the Corolla, the best-selling nameplate in history, turns 60. As always, every story carries a status line, because a final count, a forecast and a promise in a press release are not the same kind of news.

Autonomy · Toyota and Waymo

Announced October 30 · testing in Japan from 2027, then the UK · no vehicle numbers, cities or costs given · self-driving Toyotas for private owners are only being "explored"

Toyota Will Build Waymo's Next Robotaxi in the Plant It Opened for the First Corolla

Custom bZ4Xs will be assembled and fitted with Waymo's self-driving hardware under one roof in Toyota City. Until now, every Waymo has been built by someone else and converted afterward.

TOYOTA CITY, Japan — Toyota and Waymo said on October 30 that Toyota will build a custom version of its bZ4X electric SUV for Waymo's robotaxi service at its Takaoka plant in Aichi Prefecture. "The entire process will take place under one roof, from assembling the base vehicle to integrating Waymo's AV hardware," the companies said. The robotaxi version gets more rear legroom, automatic doors, a power liftgate and ambient lighting. Testing begins in Japan in 2027, and the UK and other Waymo markets follow in later years. "We'll start with the right-hand drive markets in Japan and the UK," Dmitri Dolgov, Waymo's co-chief executive, said, according to Reuters.

Neither company gave a number of cars, a cost or the cities. Hiroki Nakajima, Toyota's executive vice president, said operations would start with a small number of vehicles, Reuters reported. The 2 companies will also "continue to explore" self-driving technology for Toyotas that people own, which is a long way from a plan to sell one. "Safety technology makes the biggest difference when it reaches as many people as possible," Nakajima said.

Out of the conversion shop

Waymo, which gives more than 500,000 rides a week in 15 American cities, has always had its cars fitted out after an automaker finished building them. Most of its fleet is Jaguar I-Paces, a model Jaguar stopped making in 2024, fitted with sensors at a plant Waymo runs with Magna in Mesa, Arizona. Its newer Ojai is built by Zeekr in China and finished in Mesa, and a Hyundai Ioniq 5 version is still in testing. Tesla does the opposite: it designs and builds the Cybercab itself, in Texas. The plant Toyota picked has history of its own. Takaoka opened in September 1966 to build the first Corolla, which turns 60 this week (see the Special News Spotlight), and it still builds Corolla Hybrids for America, along with the RAV4 and the bZ4X.

The Carveyance take

Waymo's software has been ready to drive for years. Its problem has been getting cars, one conversion at a time. Toyota turns that into a production-line job at the world's biggest carmaker, and that's how a robotaxi stops being a science project and becomes a product.

What to watch: how many cars and which Japanese city, a date for the UK, and whether "explore" ever turns into a self-driving Toyota you can buy.

Earnings · Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz and Porsche

Results October 27–29 · Mercedes cut its forecast October 27 · Volkswagen's outlook, cut in September, is unchanged

Germany's Carmakers Have a China Problem, and Volkswagen Lost €5.9 Billion in 3 Months

VW's loss includes a €6.4 billion write-down on Porsche. Mercedes cut its forecast after its China sales fell 31%. Porsche's profit came back even though it sold 16% fewer cars.

WOLFSBURG, Germany — Volkswagen Group reported an operating loss of €5.9 billion (about $6.6 billion) for the third quarter on October 29, on revenue down 6.3% to €75.3 billion (about $84.3 billion). Most of the loss came from €7.8 billion (about $8.7 billion) of one-off charges, led by a non-cash €6.4 billion (about $7.2 billion) write-down of the goodwill it carries for Porsche, after Porsche lowered its own long-term profit plan. About €1 billion more was written off on assets in China. Deliveries fell 14.3% to 1.885 million, and in China they fell 38.5%, to 405,800.

"We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively," said Arno Antlitz, the chief financial officer. "At the same time, US tariffs weigh on us, the Chinese market is shrinking, and competitive pressure in Europe is increasing significantly." Volkswagen kept the forecast it cut in September, an operating margin of up to 1% this year, and is running a cost program of about €31 billion (about $34.7 billion). The next day, Reuters reported that the VW brand had suspended development work on the electric Golf. "We simply can't afford this work right now," Thomas Schäfer, the brand's chief executive, wrote to staff.

Mercedes and Porsche

Mercedes-Benz cut its forecast on October 27. It now expects group operating profit about level with last year's €5.8 billion (about $6.5 billion), instead of well above it, and a margin of 2% to 3% for its car business. In the third quarter its car sales fell 8% to 407,232, its sales in China fell 31% to about 86,800, and the car division's adjusted operating profit halved, to €560 million (about $627 million). "Market conditions have become even more challenging over the course of the year, particularly in China," said Ola Källenius, the chief executive.

Porsche, which reported on October 27, went the other way. Its operating profit for the first 9 months rose to €1.74 billion (about $1.95 billion), from €40 million a year earlier, when it booked about €2.7 billion of restructuring costs, even though deliveries fell 16% to 178,532 and in China 33%, to 21,493. Much lower restructuring costs, a €593 million (about $664 million) gain on its Bugatti Rimac stake, and higher prices and a richer mix did the work. Jochen Breckner, the chief financial officer, ruled out building Porsches in America if Audi builds its planned plant in Georgia: "The business case would not be advantageous for us, given the complexity of our product range," he told analysts, according to The Truth About Cars.

China itself is shrinking. Retail car sales there fell 21.7% in the first 9 months, according to the China Passenger Car Association, and in September Chinese brands took 69.8% of the market to the German brands' 12.2%. Even BYD, China's biggest carmaker, is growing mostly abroad: its third-quarter profit rose 28%, to 10.02 billion yuan (about $1.5 billion), short of analysts' forecasts, as its exports more than doubled to 550,704 cars. On October 27 it launched a new Qin Plus DM-i plug-in hybrid sedan from an introductory 76,900 yuan (about $11,500), with lidar-based driver assistance as an option.

The Carveyance take

For 20 years, China paid for a lot of Germany's car industry. Now Chinese brands sell cheaper cars with more technology, and the Germans are answering in 3 different ways: Volkswagen by cutting €31 billion and weighing Chinese-developed electronics for its European cars, Porsche by selling fewer, pricier cars, and Mercedes by insisting it can't walk away. None of them is selling more cars in China.

What to watch: Volkswagen's wage talks with the IG Metall union, which restart November 24, and whether VW moves its European cars onto Chinese-developed electronics.

Earnings and electric trucks · Ford

Third-quarter results October 28 · Fathom home-power details October 27 · the Fathom goes on sale in 2027, no preorders yet

Ford's Off-Road Trims Pay the Bills, and Its $28,350 Electric Truck Learns to Power a House

Ford raised the bottom of its profit outlook while its EV business lost $1.1 billion in 3 months. A day earlier, it explained how its cheapest electric pickup will keep the lights on in a blackout.

DEARBORN, Mich. — Ford earned $2.0 billion in the third quarter on revenue of $49.5 billion, down 2%, and its adjusted operating profit rose 3%, to $2.7 billion. Ford Pro, the commercial business, made $1.7 billion and Ford Blue, the gasoline and hybrid business, $1.4 billion, both down from a year earlier. Model e, the EV business, lost $1.1 billion, 25% less than a year ago. Ford raised the low end of its full-year outlook for adjusted operating profit to $10.5 billion to $11 billion, from $10 billion to $11 billion, and said Super Duty production has started at its Oakville plant in Ontario. "Our higher-margin off-road passion products accounted for about 1/4 of our U.S. sales in Q3," Sherry House, the chief financial officer, told analysts. She said the fires at Novelis, the aluminum supplier whose New York plant burned twice last year, have cost Ford about $1 billion in temporary costs this year, and that "the recovery is largely behind us."

A truck that keeps the lights on

The day before, Ford explained how the Fathom, the electric pickup it named in August with a starting price of $28,350, will power a house. It will be able to send more than 10 kW of AC power, Ford projects, against 9.6 kW from the F-150 Lightning, and because the inverter is built into the truck, it doesn't need the separate wall-mounted unit the Lightning's system used. Owners will still need Ford's Home Power Station, which Ford expects to cost about half as much as its first-generation bidirectional charger, and for outages a Home Backup Power Panel at least 60% cheaper than its first-generation backup hardware. Ford's percentages work out to about $650 for the charger and about $2,100 for the full backup kit, before installation, figures TechCrunch reported, against $5,205 for the Lightning's kit. Nor has it given the battery size or range. On the earnings call, Jim Farley, the chief executive, said, "The launch remains on track for fourth quarter next year."

The Carveyance take

Ford's profit still comes from trucks with big tires and aggressive names, and its EV unit still loses about $1 billion a quarter. The Fathom is Ford's attempt to give a cheap EV a reason to exist beyond fuel savings: a generator in the driveway that also drives to work.

What to watch: prices for the Home Power Station and backup panel, the Fathom's range and battery size, and when preorders open.

Trade · Canada and the United States

The 50% rate for January 1 was announced in August and hasn't been formalized · talks continue · no deal as of November 2

A 50% Tariff on Canadian-Built Cars Is 2 Months Away, Unless There's a Deal

The RAV4, CR-V, Civic, Pacifica and now Ford's Super Duty are built in Ontario. Honda called the increase "catastrophic." On November 1, Canada's prime minister said both sides would work toward a deal "in the coming weeks."

DETROIT — The US tariff on cars and trucks from Canada is 25%, and for vehicles that qualify under the USMCA trade agreement it's charged only on the parts that weren't made in America. That puts the effective rate at about 13%, by Global Trade Alert's estimate, or 15% to 20%, by TD Economics'. In August, after talks broke down, President Trump said the tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, parts and steel would rise to 50% on January 1, 2027. No formal order has been published, but the industry is treating the date as real. "That really would be catastrophic just for the entire industry," Jennifer Thomas, senior vice president of corporate affairs at American Honda, said at the Automotive USA conference in Detroit on October 27. "I am cautiously optimistic that cooler heads will prevail."

The exposure is concentrated. Canada builds about 1.2 million cars a year, Reuters reported, citing Barclays, and about 90% of its production is shipped to the US, according to TD Economics. Toyota and Honda build more than 3 in 4 of them: Canadian-built cars were almost 1 in 4 of Honda's US sales and 17% of Toyota's, according to Barclays. Ford has just added to its exposure, starting Super Duty production at Oakville, Ontario (story 3).

Talks are moving, slowly. Reuters reported on October 27 that the 2 governments were working on a deal to ease the steel and auto tariffs, and the next day a Canadian official said there had been "limited progress." On November 1, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he'd had a constructive conversation with Trump. "Our teams will now be working in the coming weeks to deliver that outcome," he wrote. Neither side has announced terms.

The Carveyance take

Some of America's best-selling cars aren't built in America, and many of the parts in its American-built cars cross the border more than once. A 50% tariff wouldn't just raise the price of a RAV4. It would make automakers decide where to build it, and that takes years, not 2 months.

What to watch: whether a deal lands before January 1, and whether the 50% rate is ever put into a formal order.

Hybrids and the stock market · General Motors

Plant plans announced October 27 · GM hasn't named the models or a date; the Traverse, Acadia and Enclave are from Reuters' sources · Nasdaq trading starts November 17

GM Gets Its Biggest Crossover Plant Ready for Hybrids, and Leaves the NYSE

GM's only hybrid today is the Corvette E-Ray. Now the Lansing plant that builds the Traverse, Acadia and Enclave is being prepared for them, and GM's stock is moving to Nasdaq.

LANSING, Mich. — General Motors said on October 27 that it will prepare its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant in Michigan for hybrid production, using a federal manufacturing grant it originally won in 2024 to prepare its Lansing Grand River plant for EVs. The plant builds the Chevrolet Traverse, GMC Acadia and Buick Enclave, and built more than 291,000 vehicles in 2025, its most since it opened in 2006. GM didn't name the models or give a date, but people familiar with the plans told Reuters the hybrids will be versions of those 3 SUVs. GM says its investment in the Lansing area will pass $2 billion over the next several years.

It's a turn for a company that spent most of a decade betting on EVs instead. GM's only hybrid on sale in America today is the Corvette E-Ray, and its share of the US market fell to 16.6% in the first 9 months of the year, from 17.4%, Reuters reported, while Toyota and Honda gained. "We will have hybrids. They have already been added," Mary Barra, the chief executive, told analysts on October 20. "It is not going to be additional CapEx and engineering, and we will talk more about them as we get closer to the launch." John Murphy, founder of the advisory firm The MAP and a former BofA auto analyst, called it "a good step in the right direction."

From the NYSE to Nasdaq

The same day, GM said its shares will move from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq, trading there from November 17 under the same "GM" ticker. Today's General Motors has been listed on the NYSE since its initial public offering in November 2010, after the old company's bankruptcy; the old GM had traded there for nearly a century. Paul Jacobson, the chief financial officer, said GM's "technology-driven strategy" made Nasdaq "a natural home for our listing as we grow."

The Carveyance take

Toyota has sold hybrid 3-row SUVs in America for 20 years. GM's answer has been to skip straight to electric, and buyers kept walking past it to the Toyota dealer. A hybrid Traverse would be the most ordinary product decision GM has made in years, and possibly the most important one.

What to watch: which models GM names, when they arrive, and whether the hybrids reach GM's full-size pickups and SUVs too.

Earnings · Rivian

Third-quarter results October 29 · the Uber payment and 2028 robotaxis are targets

Rivian's Smaller R2 Becomes Its Best Seller in Its First Full Quarter

Deliveries hit a record and revenue rose 38%. Rivian still lost $913 million, but each car cost $12,000 less to build than the quarter before.

IRVINE, Calif. — Rivian delivered a record 19,248 vehicles in the third quarter, up 46% from 13,201 a year earlier, and the R2 did most of the lifting. "R2 is already the best-selling Rivian vehicle, outselling both R1 and EDV in the third quarter," the company said, meaning the larger R1 SUV and pickup and the electric delivery van it builds for Amazon and others. Revenue rose 38%, to $2.155 billion, and Rivian made a gross profit of $176 million. The net loss was $913 million, down from $1.17 billion a year earlier.

The cost of building each vehicle fell by more than $12,000 from the second quarter, Reuters reported, and Rivian has added a second shift for the R2 at its plant in Normal, Illinois. The launch edition of the R2 costs $57,990, and cheaper versions down to about $45,000 are still to come. Rivian raised the low end of its delivery forecast for the year to 67,000 to 70,000, from 65,000 to 70,000. Its software and services revenue, $605 million, included $354 million from its joint venture with Volkswagen.

"We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter," said RJ Scaringe, the founder and chief executive. He also said Rivian is "very confident" it will reach an autonomy milestone this year that releases $250 million of Uber's planned investment, Reuters reported, and the 2 companies are aiming for driverless R2s on Uber's network from 2028.

The Carveyance take

Rivian made its name on a $70,000-plus truck and SUV. Its future depends on a smaller, cheaper one, and in its first full quarter the R2 outsold everything else Rivian makes. The next test is making money on each one.

What to watch: Rivian's Autonomy and AI Day on December 9, and when the cheaper R2 versions arrive.

Safety rules · NHTSA

Announced October 26 · the start of a rulemaking, not a new rule · comments and committee applications due November 26

America Starts Its First Big Rewrite of the Tire Rules in More Than 20 Years

Cars got heavier, wheels got bigger and airless tires got real. NHTSA wants the tests to catch up, and it's asking the industry to help write them.

WASHINGTON — NHTSA said on October 26 that it will modernize the federal tire safety standards, the first major overhaul in more than 20 years. Instead of drafting a rule and asking for comments afterward, it will use negotiated rulemaking: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy will appoint up to 18 people from tire makers, automakers, safety groups, research institutions and engineering associations to work out the details first.

The list covers most of what a tire has to survive. NHTSA wants new test methods for strength, rim resistance and endurance, safety requirements for new designs such as airless tires, modern sidewall markings and a review of the weight limits for trucks and SUVs. "As American tire technology and vehicle design continue to evolve, our regulatory framework must keep pace," said Jonathan Morrison, NHTSA's administrator.

The notice, published in the Federal Register on October 27, names the 3 standards in play: FMVSS 109, 119 and 139, which hold the strength, bead-unseating and endurance tests. The newest of them, FMVSS 139, was written in 2003 under the TREAD Act, which Congress passed after the Ford Explorer and Firestone tire failures that NHTSA linked to 271 deaths in America by 2001. Comments and applications to join the committee are due November 26, in docket NHTSA-2026-1717, and the committee has up to 2 years to make its recommendations.

The Carveyance take

Tires are the only part of a car that touches the road, and they now carry heavier SUVs, pickups and EVs on bigger, lower-profile wheels than the tests were written for. The question for buyers is whether tougher tests make replacement tires better, more expensive or both.

What to watch: who's named to the committee, and whether airless tires get a path to ordinary passenger cars.

Enthusiasts · Aston Martin

Revealed October 27 · shown at the Concours at Wynn in Las Vegas · no price · deliveries from the third quarter of 2027

Aston Martin Takes the Roof Off a 1,064-HP Hybrid

The Valhalla Spider does 217 mph with the roof off or the hardtop on. Put the fabric roof up and it's limited to 124 mph.

LAS VEGAS — Aston Martin revealed the Valhalla Spider on October 27, an open version of its mid-engined plug-in hybrid supercar, and showed it at the Concours at Wynn that weekend. It keeps the coupe's twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 and 3 electric motors, for a combined 1,064 hp and 811 lb-ft sent to all 4 wheels, and Aston Martin claims 0 to 62 mph in 2.5 seconds. It weighs 1,680 kg (3,704 lb) dry with the lightweight options, 25 kg (55 lb) more than the coupe, evo reported.

The roof decides the top speed. With the roof off and the clip-in wind deflector fitted, or with the carbon-fiber hardtop, which is standard on American cars, Aston Martin claims an electronically limited 217 mph. With the fabric roof, it's 124 mph. Andrew Kay, the chief engineer, told evo the hard part was airflow to the engine's roof-mounted snorkel: "The car doesn't work unless you feed that snorkel with air." It's the fastest open-top Aston Martin yet. Only 999 Valhallas will be built, coupes and Spiders together, and the company expects about 1 in 4 to be Spiders. It hasn't given a price. "High speed or low speed. Rain or shine. Roof on or roof off. Road or track. Valhalla Spider ticks every box," said Adrian Hallmark, the chief executive.

The Carveyance take

Every open supercar is a negotiation between the wind and the numbers. Aston Martin's answer is to let the owner choose: a hardtop for the 217-mph days, and a fabric roof for the days when you'd rather hear the V8 than outrun it.

Special News Spotlight

The Corolla Turns 60, Still the Best-Selling Car of All Time

Toyota built a plant just for it in 1966. More than 57 million later, it's sold in 150 countries, and that same plant has just won Waymo's robotaxi.

TOYOTA CITY, Japan — On November 5, 1966, Toyota put the first Corolla on sale in Japan: a 2-door sedan with a new 1,077 cc 4-cylinder engine making 60 PS. The Standard model cost ¥432,000 in Tokyo, about $1,200 at the time and about $12,500 in today's money. Nissan's Sunny had arrived that April with a 1,000 cc engine, so Toyota advertised the Corolla's extra 100 cc, and the launch events drew more than 1.3 million visitors. Toyota had built a new plant for it, Takaoka, which opened that September. Tatsuo Hasegawa, who led the project, wanted an economy car that scored "80 points or higher in all aspects."

It reached America in the spring of 1968, at about $1,700, or about $16,500 today. Toyota says it became the best-selling car model in history in 1997, and it sold its 50 millionth Corolla in July 2021. Its latest count is more than 57 million, sold in 150 countries and built in 12 plants, across 12 generations. Americans bought 248,088 Corollas last year, plus 99,798 Corolla Crosses. "We worked to create popular demand with the Corolla, and in my opinion, that's just what we did," said Eiji Toyoda, who later ran the company.

The Carveyance take

The Corolla never won by being exciting, and it never had to. It won by being the car you didn't have to think about, in 150 countries, for 60 years. That's harder than it looks, and nobody else has done it as many times.

Car Culture · The Corolla at 60The Car That Carried the WorldIt was never meant to be exotic or a status symbol. It became the car that let millions of people build the lives they imagined.

Safety Notices

4 recalls from this week. Repairs are free, and you can check any car by its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

Toyota Sienna Hybrid: seat backs
228,367 7-passenger Sienna Hybrids from the 2022 to 2026 model years. In some frontal crashes, a second-row seat back can unlock and fold, so it may not hold its passenger in place. Dealers will update the software in the airbag control unit, and about 200 vans with the Mobility as a Service package get new seat backs. Owner letters go out from December 7. NHTSA campaign 26V690.
Audi Q4 e-tron: battery fire risk
9,048 Q4 e-tron and Q4 Sportback e-tron SUVs from the 2024 and 2025 model years. Some high-voltage batteries, made by SK On in Hungary, may not meet quality standards, and with certain charging patterns above 80%, the battery could overheat and catch fire. Owners whose battery data is concerning or missing will be told to keep charging to 80% or less until there's a fix, which is still being developed. No fires have been reported. NHTSA campaign 26V698.
Lincoln hybrids: shift to neutral
11,623 Nautilus Hybrids from the 2026 and 2027 model years and Corsair Hybrids from 2027. Anti-rust oil from the assembly line can corrode a circuit board in the park module, and the transmission can shift into neutral while driving. Dealers will replace the module. Owner letters go out from November 2. Ford recall 26S75.
Koenigsegg CC850: all 7 of them
Every CC850 delivered in America. The electronic parking brake may not engage; one owner's car rolled away after he got out. The fix is a software update, over the air or at a dealer. NHTSA campaign 26V694.

Also That Week

6 more stories worth knowing, in brief.

Earnings · Stellantis

Third-quarter results October 28 · 2026 forecast confirmed

Stellantis Cuts Its Loss by 90%

AMSTERDAM — Stellantis lost €453 million (about $507 million) in the third quarter, 90% less than a year earlier, when it booked large charges, on revenue up 1% to €37.6 billion (about $42.1 billion). Its shipments fell 1%, by its October 13 estimate, while sales rose 1% in both North America and Europe. It expects US tariffs to cost about €1.0 billion (about $1.1 billion) this year, and Antonio Filosa, the chief executive, said it expects "positive Industrial Free Cash Flow in 2027."

Why it matters: the maker of Jeep, Ram and Dodge is losing far less money, but it isn't making any yet.

Technology · Volkswagen

Reported October 26 by Manager Magazin and October 28 by Reuters · no decision announced

Volkswagen Weighs Chinese-Developed Electronics for Its European Cars

WOLFSBURG, Germany — Volkswagen is studying whether to put CEA, the electronic architecture it developed with Xpeng in China, under its future mass-market Volkswagens, Skodas and Cupras in Europe, Reuters reported, following Manager Magazin, which put the share at about 75% of those models and the saving at €4 billion to €5 billion. Volkswagen already uses CEA in 5 China-built EVs. The risk is to its software partnership with Rivian, worth up to $5.8 billion, which was meant to supply the electronics for its cars outside China.

Why it matters: for decades, technology flowed from Germany to China. This would send it the other way.

Business · Toyota

September figures October 29 · the engine plan reported October 28 by Automotive News

Toyota's Sales Slip Again, and It Wants to Sell Engines to Rivals

TOYOTA CITY, Japan — Toyota's global sales fell 2.2% in September to 860,107, Reuters reported, with China down for an 8th month in a row. Separately, Automotive News reported that Toyota plans to sell its new 1.5-liter and 2.0-liter 4-cylinder engines, and its next hybrid systems from as early as 2027, to other carmakers, aiming for about €1.5 billion (about $1.7 billion) a year by 2032. Toyota hasn't named customers.

Why it matters: while others are cutting engine programs, Toyota is betting there's money in being the industry's engine supplier.

Launches · Mazda

2027 lineup announced October 27

Mazda Drops the CX-70 for a 2-Row CX-90

IRVINE, Calif. — The CX-70, a 2-row version of the CX-90 that arrived in 2024, is gone. For 2027 the CX-90 itself comes with 2 or 3 rows, from $41,345 including destination, and the 2-row version starts at $48,525, Motor1 reported.

Why it matters: a single name is cheaper to sell than 2.

Used cars · Carvana

Third-quarter results October 28

Carvana Has Its Biggest Quarter Yet

TEMPE, Ariz. — Carvana sold 217,385 used cars to customers in the third quarter, up 39%, on record revenue of $8.04 billion, and earned $483 million. "We are just beginning to realize the potential of the machine we are building," said Ernie Garcia, the founder and chief executive.

Why it matters: with new-car payments at records, more buyers are going used, and more of them are doing it online.

Collector cars · RM Sotheby's

Sold October 31, London

Ayrton Senna's Honda NSX Sells for £871,250

LONDON — The 1991 NSX that Honda provided for Senna's use in Europe sold for £871,250 (about $1.16 million) at RM Sotheby's London sale, above its estimate of £500,000 to £800,000. A Ferrari F40 modified in Japan in the style of the racing LM went for just over £2.5 million (about $3.3 million), and the top lot, a 2022 Ferrari Daytona SP3, brought £8,161,259 (about $10.9 million). The sale totaled just over £36.5 million (about $48.5 million).

Why it matters: an ordinary early NSX sells for a small fraction of that. The extra money is for the name.

Since That Week

Where last week's stories went next.

Follow-up · Tesla's Cybercab

Tesla's sworn answers to NHTSA's 21 questions about how it certified the Cybercab were due October 30. Neither Tesla nor NHTSA has said publicly whether they were filed, and NHTSA can fine a company up to $27,874 a day, to a maximum of $139,356,994, for an incomplete or false answer. The cyan-light proposal is open for comments until November 25. Read: Tesla Wants to Sell You a Car With No Steering Wheel. The Rules Aren't Ready.

Follow-up · Car payments

The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, so car-loan rates got no help from the Fed this month. The vote was 10 to 2, and both dissenters wanted a rate increase. Cox Automotive expects October sales of about 1,375,000, up 7.2%, when the figures come out this week. Read: The Price of a New Car Has Stopped Rising. The Cost of Owning One Hasn't.

Follow-up · Audi's Georgia plant

US officials promised Audi talks on tariff relief for its planned Georgia plant, Reuters reported on October 29, citing people familiar with the matter. Audi wants the 15% tariff on its European imports cut to 7.5%, and the Commerce Department is expected to agree to about 10%, the sources said. Neither has announced anything. Porsche said it won't move production to the plant (story 2).

Follow-up · Tesla's Roadster

The Roadster's cold-gas thrusters run on nitrogen stored at up to 10,000 psi, and refilling them is slow. "Current fill times are like two to six hours. We're hoping to get down to under a half hour," Lars Moravy, Tesla's vice president of vehicle engineering, said, as quoted by Motor1 on October 28.

Follow-up · Fuel prices

Regular gasoline averaged $4.17 a gallon on November 2, down from $4.29 a week earlier, according to AAA. A year ago it was $3.04. Diesel averaged $6.29.

Worth Watching

Not big stories yet, but they could be.

SEMA, this week
The aftermarket's biggest show runs November 3 to 6 at the Las Vegas Convention Center, and opens with Jay Leno in conversation with Harley-Davidson's chief executive, Artie Starrs.
October sales
Due this week. Cox Automotive forecasts about 1,375,000 new vehicles, up 7.2% from a year ago, a seasonally adjusted annual pace of about 16.1 million.
A car that coaches you
Maserati showed Track Assist, a "digital trainer" that manages braking and acceleration to teach braking points and apex speed. It joins Maserati's driving school in 2027: driver assistance meant to make you a better driver, not to replace you.
A truck that feeds the grid
In a 3-year research project, an electric MAN eTGX sent up to 350 kW back to the grid and cut energy costs by about 10% on average. MAN is working to bring it to production, with no date.

News Versus Noise

How solid is each story? Our ledger for the week.

Confirmed
Toyota and Waymo's plan to build the bZ4X at Takaoka. The results from Volkswagen, Mercedes, Porsche, Ford, Rivian, BYD, Stellantis and Carvana, and Mercedes's lower forecast. GM's Lansing plant plans and its move to Nasdaq. NHTSA's tire rulemaking. The Valhalla Spider's specifications. The 4 recalls. The Fed's decision. Senna's NSX sale.
Reported, not confirmed
The Traverse, Acadia and Enclave as GM's first new hybrids, from Reuters' sources. Volkswagen's study of Chinese-developed electronics for Europe, from Manager Magazin and Reuters. Toyota's plan to sell engines to other carmakers, from Automotive News. Audi's tariff-relief talks, from Reuters' sources. Volkswagen's pause on the electric Golf, from an internal memo seen by Reuters.
Plans without dates
Toyota and Waymo's UK launch, and anything for private owners. The models and timing of GM's hybrids. Prices for the Fathom's home-power hardware. A price for the Valhalla Spider.
Not final yet
The 50% tariff on Canadian cars, announced in August but not formalized, and any deal to avoid it. Cox's October forecast. Rivian's Uber milestone and 2028 robotaxis, both targets. NHTSA's tire standards, which are at the start of a rulemaking.
Noise
An electric Ford Escape: first reported by Ford Authority in May, and Ford calls it speculation. Aurora's "order" for 500 driverless trucks from Charger Logistics: a nonbinding memorandum, and Aurora itself warns it may not become firm orders "on the anticipated timeframe or at all." Self-driving Toyotas for sale: Toyota and Waymo will only "explore" them. GM joining the Nasdaq-100: possible, not promised. And the Valhalla Spider's price: magazine estimates range from about £935,000 to more than £1.3 million, and Aston Martin hasn't said.
